Common Ground · Living Mapmaker

A living map woven by the people who move through a place. Built against the Loom of Legends reference drawings, one gauntlet wave at a time.

wave 2 · living-mapmaker.html — 2026-08-08 03:36 UTC — wave 2 of the loop

single largest remaining gap

The weave still reads as very good drawing on a very good map, not yet as one cloth: the drawn city and the threads occupy the same plane instead of the threads lying in a ground that has its own tooth and shadow.

Carried forward from the wave 2 visual verdict. Fibre quality, interlacing and palette are now at the bar; what remains is the relationship between the weave and the paper it sits on — the reference sells cloth partly through ground shadow and a fabric that dents the surface it lies on.

Critic verdicts

Wave 1 five critics, fresh context

  • first touch The cold screen was empty and taught nothing; the ghost read as a GPS breadcrumb and left nothing behind. closed
  • map feel Pan inertia came from one untimed event and decayed per frame, so a careful drag threw the map 272 px and could not be stopped. closed
  • visual language Authorship used an eight-hue categorical palette, so a busy ground became a multi-series line chart. closed
  • weaving and return The weave came from polyline intersections, so it was driven by GPS jitter: 0 m of jitter produced nothing, 2 m produced a rope of landmark knots. closed
  • functional gauntlet All tabs on a device shared one identity: same-device sync was silently dead and two tabs minted the same op id for different strokes, losing work permanently. closed

Wave 2 four critics, fresh context

  • first touch The demonstration never actually crossed: the knot bloomed on a point the first thread came nowhere near. closed
  • visual language Threads were constant-width vector ribbons with a uniform casing and no interlacing, so the ground read as a flow diagram. partial
  • weaving and return Weight came to exactly three times the thread count whatever the number of people, so one person's habit drew identically to a shared commons. closed
  • functional gauntlet A single malformed op left a permanently black screen that survived reload. closed

Notes

Outbound internet is blocked in the build sandbox, so every screenshot here is the artifact in its offline state: the Atlanta geometry you see is real OpenStreetMap data compiled into the file itself, not raster tiles. On a phone with a network, tiles fade in underneath the ink and the map carries you anywhere.

Cross-device collaboration was verified against a real MQTT broker running locally, including late join, concurrent drawing, and reconnect convergence. In the wild the ground races three public brokers; if none answer, everything still works on the device and between its tabs.

The critics could not see the original reference drawings, which exist only in the conversation. They worked from a written reference brief describing each of the eight sheets.
